newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money firms at 9.0/9.5 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money firms at 9.0/9.5 percent.

text.p: Jakarta call money firmed at 9.0/9.5 percent on Wednesday amid ample supply, dealers said.
One foreign bank dealer said liquidity was sufficient but the rates were firm because of an uptrend in short-dated swaps due to month-end liquidity worries.
The dealer said longer-term rates were edging up slightly as over-the-month money increased. Spot/next swap rose to 1.45 points from 1.3 points at the opening.
One- and three-month money were quoted at 13.5/13.75 and 14.50/14.75 percent, respectively.

The central bank did not offer overnight papers (SBIs), but offered seven-day SBIs at 11.75 percent, 14-day at 12.0 percent, one-month at 11.75 percent, three-month at 13.75 percent, six-month at 14.0 percent and 12-month at 14.5 percent.
The average overnight interbank rate on Tuesday was 10.81 percent, compared with 10.13 percent on Monday.
